paragraphs.paragraph: Longing for God in the Wilderness
paragraphs.title: Longing for God in the Wilderness

answers: In a dry and thirsty land
easy.explanation: David describes the land as dry and thirsty, where no water is.
easy.q: Where does David say he is seeking God?

easy.explanation: He says, "my soul thirsteth for thee."
easy.q: What does David's soul thirst for?

easy.explanation: David says he wants to see God's power and glory.
easy.q: What does David want to see in the sanctuary?

medium.explanation: Physical thirst is used to express David's intense spiritual longing for God.
medium.q: What does the image of thirst express in this passage?

medium.explanation: David says, "my flesh longeth for thee."
medium.q: What does David say his flesh longs for?

answers: A dry land is contrasted with the vision of God's power and glory
The king is contrasted with the foxes
medium.explanation: The wilderness is dry and without water, while David desires to behold God's glory in the sanctuary.
medium.q: What contrast is presented in these verses?

answers: Its dryness intensifies his longing for God
It proves that David has forgotten God
It shows that David seeks only physical water
challenge.explanation: The harsh, waterless setting makes David's spiritual thirst especially vivid.
challenge.q: Why is the wilderness setting important to David's expression of faith?

answers: He longs for God's presence and majesty
He wants to escape all worship
He is interested only in the sanctuary building
challenge.explanation: Seeing God's power and glory represents a desire for God's presence and majesty.
challenge.q: What does David's desire to see God in the sanctuary reveal?

answers: Seeking God, thirsting for Him, and longing to behold His glory
Fleeing from God, fighting enemies, and celebrating victory
Finding water, leaving the wilderness, and returning home
challenge.explanation: The verses move from seeking God to expressing thirst and longing to see His glory.
challenge.q: Which progression best summarizes the passage?

paragraphs.idea: Longing for God in the Wilderness

easy.explanation: David declares that God's lovingkindness is better than life.
easy.q: What does David say is better than life?

easy.explanation: He says, "I will lift up my hands in thy name."
easy.q: What does David lift up in God's name?

easy.explanation: David compares the satisfaction of his soul to marrow and fatness.
easy.q: With what will David's soul be satisfied?

answers: He will complain about the wilderness
medium.explanation: Because God's lovingkindness is better than life, David says his lips will praise Him.
medium.q: How will David respond to God's lovingkindness?

medium.explanation: Lifting the hands in God's name expresses prayer and worship.
medium.q: What do lifted hands most naturally express in this context?

medium.explanation: Joyful lips are lips that praise God with gladness.
medium.q: What does the phrase "joyful lips" describe?

answers: He values God's covenant love above earthly life
He believes life has no value at all
He desires wealth more than God's mercy
challenge.explanation: David places God's lovingkindness above life itself.
challenge.q: What does the statement that lovingkindness is better than life show about David's priorities?

answers: The richness of food illustrates the fullness David finds in God
Physical food is condemned as sinful
David says that thirst is better than satisfaction
challenge.explanation: Marrow and fatness provide an image for the deep satisfaction of praising God.
challenge.q: How are physical and spiritual satisfaction connected in these verses?

answers: Recognizing God's goodness, blessing Him, and praising Him joyfully
Leaving the sanctuary, hiding his hands, and becoming silent
Seeking enemies, defeating them, and taking their possessions
challenge.explanation: David recognizes God's lovingkindness, blesses Him, lifts his hands, and praises Him with joyful lips.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes David's response?

paragraphs.paragraph: Remembering God and Dwelling Under His Protection
paragraphs.title: Remembering God and Dwelling Under His Protection

easy.explanation: David says, "When I remember thee upon my bed."
David says, "thou hast been my help."
easy.q: What has God been to David?

easy.explanation: He says, "My soul followeth hard after thee."
easy.q: What does David's soul follow closely?

medium.explanation: David meditates on God in the night watches.
medium.q: When does David meditate on God?

answers: The lower parts of the earth
medium.explanation: The shadow of God's wings is an image of shelter and protection.

answers: Because God has been his help
Because he wants to hide from worship
Because he has found earthly riches
medium.explanation: David connects his rejoicing with God's help and protection.
medium.q: Why does David rejoice under the shadow of God's wings?

answers: Meditation on God strengthens David's devotion to Him
Nighttime remembrance causes David to reject God
challenge.explanation: Remembering and meditating on God leads to a soul that follows closely after Him.
challenge.q: What connection exists between remembering God at night and following Him closely?

answers: It shows that David is hiding from God
challenge.explanation: God's right hand represents His power and support for David.
challenge.q: What does the phrase "thy right hand upholdeth me" add to the passage?

answers: Remembering God, rejoicing in His protection, and clinging to Him
Fearing the night, fleeing the sanctuary, and seeking wealth
Fighting enemies, losing hope, and abandoning prayer
challenge.explanation: David remembers and meditates on God, rejoices under His protection, and follows Him closely.
challenge.q: Which progression best summarizes these verses?

paragraphs.idea: Remembering God and Dwelling Under His Protection

paragraphs.paragraph: The Enemies and the Silencing of Liars
paragraphs.title: The Enemies and the Silencing of Liars

easy.explanation: The verse says they seek David's soul to destroy it.
easy.q: What do those who seek David's soul want to do?

answers: Into the lower parts of the earth
easy.explanation: David says they shall go into the lower parts of the earth.
The passage says, "the king shall rejoice in God."
easy.q: In whom will the king rejoice?

answers: They will fall by the sword
medium.explanation: David says, "They shall fall by the sword."
medium.q: What will happen to those who seek David's soul?

answers: Their lying speech will be silenced
medium.explanation: A stopped mouth represents the ending of their false speech.
medium.q: What does it mean that the liars' mouths shall be stopped?

medium.explanation: The verse says, "every one that sweareth by him shall glory."
medium.q: What will everyone who swears by God do?

answers: The king rejoices in God while liars are silenced
The wilderness is compared with the sanctuary
The night watches are compared with the morning
challenge.explanation: Those loyal to God rejoice and glory, while those who speak lies are stopped.
challenge.q: What contrast appears at the end of the psalm?

answers: It portrays their complete defeat and dishonor
It shows that they have become powerful rulers
It means they have safely escaped
challenge.explanation: The image of bodies becoming food for foxes emphasizes the enemies' defeat.
challenge.q: What is the significance of the enemies becoming a portion for foxes?

answers: The faithful glory in God, while the liars are silenced
The faithful are silenced, while the liars rejoice
challenge.explanation: The verse places those who honor God on one side and lying speakers on the other.
challenge.q: What distinction is made between those who swear by God and those who speak lies?

paragraphs.idea: The Enemies and the Silencing of Liars
